# Module 6: Job delivery and scheduling

*From won job to handover with the paperwork keeping up, not the other way round.*

**Who does it in a small business:** Owner, project manager, office admin.

## The typical process

Every business does it a bit differently. This is the common shape we see.

| # | Step | What happens | Tools | Where time goes |
|:-:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Set up the job | Job in the system, folders, the handover | simPRO, ServiceM8, SharePoint | copy-paste |
| 2 | Book the crew | Dates, crew and subbies, client told | Field app, SMS, Excel |  |
| 3 | Paperwork before start | SWMS, inductions, compliance checks | Word, PDF | slow |
| 4 | On site | Progress, photos and issues in group chats | WhatsApp, Phone |  |
| 5 | Report and claim | Weekly client report, variations, progress claim | Excel, Word, Outlook | slow |
| 6 | Finish and hand over | Defects, photos, close-out (module 9) | Paper, PDF | slow |

## Where the time goes

From businesses APG has audited, anonymised. Hours are staff estimates, not measurements.

- Project managers spend up to 80% of their week on admin
- Site updates in WhatsApp turned into data by hand: about 10 h a week per person
- A weekly client report: about 3.5 h per active job
- A progress claim: half a day to a day per job per month

## Step 1: the intake

"How we do it" (planned): Map a job from won to handed over: who sets it up, how the crew is booked, and what gets reported.

It hands back your own version of the map above, with your tools and your hours, then suggests which skill to build first.

## The skills

- **Job setup pack** (connected): Folders, job and checklist made from the won quote
- **Site update to report** (connected): Voice notes and photos become the weekly client report
- **Defects from a site walk** (connected): Record the walk; the defect list is drafted. Being built
